moon.geology: Longest basalt lava tube cave system in Southeast Asia (>25 km, 50+ tubes) in Dak Nong UNESCO Geopark. Thick basalt roof preserves stable temperature (20-22°C / 295 K) and shields cosmic radiation, ideal for testing autonomous SLAM rovers and subsurface lunar habitats.
moon.limits: Tropical monsoon surface weathering, 1g Earth gravity (6x lunar gravity), atmospheric moisture, and absence of ultra-high vacuum conditions.

mars.geology: Arsia Mons shield volcano hosts collapsed pit chains and skylights entering sub-surface lava tubes. Krong No's basalt tubes provide structural analog for testing robotic tethering and subterranean exploration on Mars.
mars.limits: Earth atmospheric density (96 kPa vs 0.6 kPa on Mars), seasonal rainfall, vegetation cover, and absence of perchlorate dust.

moon.mineralText: High-Ti Mare Basalt, Pyroclastic Black Beads
moon.geology: Timanfaya's young basaltic volcanic fields and Cueva de los Verdes lava tube serve as premier ESA PANGAEA testing ground for lunar astronaut EVA exploration and lunar pyroclastic basalt mapping.
moon.limits: Oceanic island moisture, salt spray, and atmospheric pressure contrast with lunar hard vacuum.

mars.geology: Young basaltic volcanic landscape in Timanfaya National Park featuring extensive lava flows, cinder cones, and lava tubes. Extensively used for rover traction testing, volcanic geology mapping, and planetary cave exploration training (ESA PANGAEA).
mars.limits: Maritime island climate, oceanic air humidity, biological colonization, and weathering processes contrast with the arid, cold, low-pressure Martian environment.

moon.mineralText: Lunar Impact Breccia, Anorthositic Shocked Melt
moon.geology: Classic simple-to-complex impact crater analog where Apollo astronauts trained to identify shocked minerals, shatter cones, and impact ejecta blankets on the Moon.
moon.limits: Target rock is sedimentary limestone/sandstone whereas lunar highlands are anorthositic crystalline crust.

mars.geology: Best-preserved meteorite impact crater on Earth (~50,000 years old, 1.2 km diameter). High-energy kinetic impact physics mirror Martian impact structures explored by the Curiosity and Opportunity rovers.
mars.limits: Dense terrestrial atmosphere, aeolian and fluvial weathering, 1g gravity, and target lithology differs from Martian basaltic crust.

earth.mineralText: Pahoehoe & Aa Basalt, Scoria, Pyroxene, Plagioclase

moon.geology: Extensive Holocene basaltic lava field along the Great Rift of Idaho with pahoehoe and aa lava flows, spatter cones, and collapsed lava tube caves. Key analog for lunar mare volcanic features and basaltic morphology.
moon.limits: Terrestrial subaerial lava emplacement with 1 atm air and meteoric water interaction; lunar lavas erupted in vacuum with much lower viscosity.

mars.geology: Massive fissure-fed basalt plains with extensive pressure ridges, squeeze-ups, and inflated pahoehoe sheets directly analogous to Martian volcanic plains in Daedalia Planum.
mars.limits: Seasonal winter snow cover, high atmospheric oxygen, and biological lichen growth on lava surfaces.

moon.geology: Barren, treeless high-altitude mountain valley landscape simulating lunar highland terrain navigation and extreme solar UV exposure.
moon.limits: Terrestrial lacustrine sediments contain clay and carbonates formed by liquid water, unlike desiccated lunar silicates.

mars.geology: High-altitude cold desert 'Moonland' paleolake basin in the Himalayas (~3,500 m elevation). Fine-grained clay lacustrine sediments and deeply dissected badlands landscape provide prime analog for ancient Martian deltaic and paleolake environments.
mars.limits: Tectonic uplift rates, higher terrestrial atmospheric density, and summer seasonal rainfall differ from hyperarid modern Mars.

earth.mineralText: Granite, Quartz, Feldspathic Regolith, Aeolian Sand

moon.geology: Heavily eroded, desiccated bedrock canyons with sharp relief and fine abrasive sand simulating lunar crater rim traverses and rover track wear.
moon.limits: Aeolian wind transport of sand requires atmosphere; lunar dust transport is driven by electrostatic levitation and micrometeoroids.

mars.geology: Hyperarid badlands canyon carved by the Swakop River combined with coastal Namib sand seas. Exemplifies wind-dominated aeolian erosion and rover mobility terrain analogous to Martian dune fields.
mars.limits: Presence of coastal fog humidity, oceanic moisture influence, terrestrial 1g gravity, and oxidizing Earth atmosphere.

name: ⭐ 7. Valle de la Luna (Atacama Desert, Chile)

moon.mineralText: Lunar Imbrium Ejecta Breccia, KREEP Basalt
moon.geology: Extreme dryness and absence of soil organic carbon provide baseline testing conditions for solar UV degradation and ultra-dry sensor calibration.
moon.limits: Earth atmosphere provides UV shielding relative to the raw lunar surface; air pressure is 76 kPa.

mars.target: NASA MARS BASELINE (VALLE DE LA LUNA)
mars.geology: Hyperarid core of the Atacama Desert, one of the driest places on Earth. Extreme ultraviolet radiation, perchlorate-bearing soils, and negligible precipitation make it NASA's primary terrestrial baseline for Martian soil astrobiology and rover instrument calibration.
mars.limits: Atmospheric pressure (76 kPa) is still two orders of magnitude higher than Mars (0.6 kPa); 1g gravity and microbial presence in deep subsurfaces.

moon.geology: Active volcanic caldera along the Mid-Atlantic Ridge featuring fresh basaltic fissure eruptions, geothermal fields, and tephra deposits. NASA Apollo geology training site (1965-1967) and benchmark for lunar mare basalt petrology.
moon.limits: Abundant glacial water, hydrothermal steam vents, subglacial volcanism, and wet atmospheric interactions absent on the desiccated Moon.

mars.mineralText: Young Martian Basalt Flows, Plagioclase, Pyroxene
mars.geology: Volcanic fissure eruptions with fresh platy-ridged flood basalts and palagonitized tephra layers analogous to young flood lava plains in Elysium Planitia on Mars.
mars.limits: Cold rainy subarctic maritime weather and geothermal ground heating differ from freezing dry Martian climate.

earth.mineralText: Halite, Gypsum, Sodium Sulfate, Anhydrite, Clay

moon.geology: Flat expanses of crustal minerals testing long-range rover dead reckoning navigation and high-contrast glare visibility.
moon.limits: Earth playa salts are aqueous precipitates; Moon has no aqueous evaporite deposits.

mars.geology: Massive endorheic salt lake (playa) in southern Tunisia rich in gypsum, halite, and clay minerals. Serves as an evaporite basin analog for ancient Martian chloride and sulfate deposits detected by Mars orbiters and rovers.
mars.limits: Seasonal flooding, shallow water table, and modern Earth atmospheric moisture contrast with long-desiccated Martian evaporite flats.

earth.mineralText: Shocked Basalt, Maskelynite, Impact Spherules, Carbonates

moon.geology: Premier terrestrial analog for hypervelocity meteorite impacts in basaltic crust, producing diaplectic glass (maskelynite) identical to Apollo lunar impact samples.
moon.limits: Crater lake water, tropical climate, and active microbial biosphere differ from lunar desiccated regolith.

mars.geology: Unique hypervelocity meteorite impact crater (~52,000 years old, 1.8 km diameter) carved entirely into Deccan Traps basaltic bedrock. Directly matches basaltic impact structures and hydrothermal alteration minerals in Jezero Crater, Mars.
mars.limits: Saline alkaline crater lake in the interior, tropical monsoon rainfall, dense vegetation, and biological ecosystem.

earth.mineralText: Andesitic Basalt, Pyroclastic Tephra, Volcanic Scoria

moon.geology: Steep composite cones and silicic volcanic domes testing robotic steep-slope climbing and ash traverse navigation.
moon.limits: Glacial ice, subduction-zone hydration, and atmospheric precipitation.

mars.geology: Subarctic volcanic wilderness with over 30 active stratovolcanoes, basaltic scoria cones, and extensive tephra plains (Tolbachik). Highly relevant analog for cold-climate Martian volcanism and rover autonomous traverse over coarse volcanic ash.
mars.limits: Subduction-zone calc-alkaline magmatism, heavy winter snowfall, glacial ice interactions, and active terrestrial biosphere.

earth.mineralText: Mudstone, Siltstone, Volcanic Ash Paleosols, Smectite

moon.mineralText: Lunar Layered Regolith and Basalt Wall Strata
moon.geology: Rhythmically bedded sedimentary cliff exposures useful for practicing stratigraphic column logging and cliffside robotic sampling.
moon.limits: Formed by fluvial river deposition on Earth; lunar rilles were carved by thermal erosion of turbulent lava flows.

mars.mineralText: Martian Rhythmic Sulfate & Smectite Clay Strata
mars.geology: Sharply eroded sedimentary pinnacles, gullies, and buttes featuring rhythmic alternating clay, siltstone, and volcanic ash paleosol layers. Directly analogous to layered sulfate and clay strata explored by the Curiosity rover at Mount Sharp, Mars.
mars.limits: Fluvial erosion driven by heavy continental rainstorms, seasonal freezing/thawing, and terrestrial vegetation.
